sections.history: Thirusemponsei, the Semponsei Koil, lies about 8 km from Sirkazhi near Thirunangur, in Chola Nadu, in what is now Mayiladuthurai district. It is one of the 108 Divya Desams sung by the Alvars in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham, and one of the eleven Thirunangur Tirupathis hymned by Thirumangai Alvar. The presiding Lord is Perarulalan Perumal, also called Sempon Arangar, standing and facing east, with the Goddess Alli Mamalar Nachiyar. Its antiquity rests on the Alvar's hymns, placed between the seventh and ninth centuries.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian temple whose sanctum is crowned by the Kanaka vimana, the golden vimana, a name that echoes the golden origin told of the temple. Its sacred waters are the Hema Pushkarini, the golden tank, with the Kanaka Theertham also named. Perarulalan Perumal stands facing east within, with Alli Mamalar Nachiyar. The names of vimana and tank alike carry the temple's theme of gold.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells that after the war in Lanka, Rama stayed with the sage Drudhanetra. On the sage's advice, to expiate the sin of having slain Ravana, a brahmin, Rama had a cow fashioned of gold and gave it to a brahmin, who used the gold to build this temple. Hence Sem-pon-sei Koil, the temple made of red gold. Devotional tradition adds that here the Lord himself provided the wealth for his own shrine.
sections.festivals: The principal festival is the Aippasi Brahmotsavam (October–November), culminating on Swati, the Perumal's birth star. The temple also joins the Thirunangur Garuda Sevai on the day after Thai Amavasai (January–February), when its utsavar goes to Thirumanimadam to meet the other lords of Thirunangur and Thirumangai Alvar's mangalasasanam is re-enacted. Tradition holds that seeing all eleven together equals visiting each.
sections.experience: Come for the story of the golden cow and the temple raised from it; the names of the vimana and tank will repeat it as you walk. The shrine is about 8 km from Sirkazhi, whose railway station is the nearest, and fits neatly into a day among the other Thirunangur Tirupathis. The Aippasi Brahmotsavam is the season to see it at its liveliest.

visit.timings: Darshan is generally held in morning and evening sessions with a midday break; the Garuda Sevai day is by far the busiest. Confirm timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Thirunangur lies about 8 km by road south-east of Sirkazhi (Sirkali) in Mayiladuthurai district. Sirkazhi, on the Chennai–Mayiladuthurai railway line, is the nearest station, and Tiruchirappalli, about 160 km away, the nearest major airport. Auto-rickshaws and taxis from Sirkazhi reach the village; the eleven shrines lie among paddy fields close to one another.
